Question: Define the following terms, making clear the distinctions between them:a) Bitb) Bytec) Word.

Options: 
A. Byte is a collection of 4 bits, Bit is the smallest unit of storage, Word is a fixed size of bytes determined by the operating system.
B. Bit is a group of 8 units, Byte is dependent upon the hardware architecture, Word is the most elementary data unit.
C. Bit is a variable-length unit of data, Byte is a standard size across all platforms, Word is the most complex unit of data.
D. Byte is a group of 10 bits, Bit is the smallest unit of measure, Word can be any number of bytes as specified by the user.
E. Byte is the elementary data unit, Bit is a group of 8 bytes, Word is dependent on the software.
F. Word is a collection of 16 bits, Bit is the largest unit of data, Byte is a fixed size of words.
G. Word is the elementary data unit, Byte is a group of 8 bits, Bit is dependent on the hardware architecture.
H. Word is a group of 1024 bits, Bit is the smallest data unit but is not used in storage, Byte is a group of 4 or 8 bits depending on the processor.
I. Bit is a group of 2 bytes, Byte is the standard unit of data transfer, Word is the amount of data that a processor can handle at one time.
J. Bit is the most elementary data unit, Byte is a group of 8 bits, Word is dependent upon the hardware architecture of the computer.

Provide the correct letter choice in \boxed{X}, where X is the correct letter choice. Keep the explanation or feedback within 3 sentences.

    *   **Word:** The amount of data that the CPU processes at once. It varies by architecture (e.g., 16-bit, 32-bit, 64-bit). Sometimes referred to as the size of a register. It is dependent on hardware architecture.
